summary: Verified milestone M4 (SLA clocks, entitlements and escalation) across its five documented steps. Verdict ready-with-findings, recorded with set-milestone --status verified. All five steps are documented, the preceding milestone:M3 gate is approved, and no step is blocked - two steps were blocked mid-build (M4-S01 checker-policy, M4-S02 ambiguity) and both blocks were closed at a SKILL rather than at an artefact, with the byte-identical rejected file passing on re-run. All five runnable milestone acceptance tests pass, run verbatim from the build directory: check_business_hours_and_holidays.py exit 0 (one INFO on the always-open Severity 1 24x7 calendar), check_entitlements_and_milestones.py --strict exit 0 (0 error/0 warning/2 info, and the W3 calendar cross-reference --strict exists for did NOT fire, so the assertion is live), check_escalation_rules.py exit 0 (W1 no-rule-active is the intended state under Q47; E2 and E7 both clear), check_entitlement_apex_hooks.py exit 0 (4 files, 0 ERROR 0 WARN), and the always-on manifest check consistent. 35 references resolved, 2 unassertable, 0 unresolved. Every recorded deploy-order position agrees with its artefact type - automation at 8, SLA at 10 - with no backwards metadata dependency. The merged manifest built clean: 6 types, 8 members, uniform version 67.0, no member collision, no version conflict. Ten findings, F-39 to F-48, two HIGH. F-40 is the one the gate must not miss: milestone M4's own goal field promises a Premier EMEA case's first-response clock runs on the EMEA calendar, and both entitlement processes pin businessHours US Support on the process AND on the milestone, so the EMEA calendar M4-S03 stamps reaches only the escalation clock - 17:00 Friday London expires at 21:00 the same Friday London on New York hours. O-M4S02-02 records the divergence; no step reads milestones[].goal, so nobody compared the two. F-39: settings/Entitlement.settings-meta.xml (enableEntitlements) is declared in no step's outputs anywhere in the plan, and the dependency is wider than O-M4S02-01 could see at M4-S02's scope - three of M4's five steps need it, because the flow names $Record.EntitlementId and the Entitlement object and the Apex names CaseMilestone and SlaProcess. Six of the ten findings are compositions of facts two different files already recorded accurately and nothing read together. Nine gate decision items presented with a recommendation each; item 9 (the RTM's 3 residual orphans) is CLOSED - check_rtm.py v1.1.5 landed today as 0c585e185 and the build-scope re-run reports 47 rows, 0 orphans, 0 gaps, 0 warnings, so the only residue is stale prose in traceability.md (F-48). The merged manifest deliberately carries NO ApexClass or ApexTrigger member: M4-S05 declares no package.xml per the Apex exception and M5-S05 aggregates its members, but M5-S05 is pending, so until it runs no manifest in this build carries the Apex and a manifest-mode dry run would deploy the SLA clocks without the trigger that stops them (F-43). No sf command, no mock_deploy.py, no org contact, no gate write, no manual test ticked, no artefact touched, nothing deployed.

findings.title: The merged M4 manifest cannot deploy itself into an org that does not already have Entitlement Management enabled
findings.detail: settings/Entitlement.settings-meta.xml carrying enableEntitlements is declared in no step's outputs[] anywhere in plan.json. O-M4S02-01 established that at M4-S02's scope and called it a gate item; what no step could see is that the dependency is wider than M4-S02's own two files. Three of M4's five steps need the feature: M4-S02's two EntitlementProcess files and the MilestoneType are the components themselves; M4-S03's flow names $Record.EntitlementId and queries the Entitlement object in Get_Active_Entitlement; M4-S05's Apex names the CaseMilestone and SlaProcess sObjects. Predicted deploy-time error per skills/devops/deployment-error-diagnosis: INVALID_TYPE: sObject type 'Entitlement' is not supported on the flow's record lookup, plus a feature-not-enabled rejection on the EntitlementProcess components - a failure whose message points at the flow rather than at the missing switch. Mock deploy run 4's 55/55 does not clear this: sfskills-dev already has the feature on, so run 4 proves the artefacts are correct, not that the manifest is self-sufficient. enableMilestoneStoppedTime rides in the same unowned file and gotchas.md #10 wants it on before go-live rather than after the first dispute.

evidence.grounded_in: decisions.md O-M4S02-01; artefacts/M4-S02/deploy-order.md section 5; artefacts/M4-S03/flows/Case_BeforeSave_StampEntitlementAndCalendar.flow-meta.xml (object Entitlement, $Record.EntitlementId); artefacts/M4-S05/classes/CaseMilestoneService.cls (CaseMilestone SOQL); reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M4.md run 4

findings.recommendation: Option (b): record enabling Entitlement Management in Setup as a named deploy prerequisite alongside F-28, with an owner and a date, naming BOTH enableEntitlements (before anything in M4 deploys) and enableMilestoneStoppedTime (before go-live). Same shape the M3 gate already accepted for F-28. Amending an M4 step's outputs[] would force a rebuild of a documented step for a file that changes nothing about the artefacts already proven.

findings.title: Milestone M4's own goal is not met: a Premier EMEA case's first-response clock runs on US Support hours, not EMEA
findings.detail: plan.json milestones[M4].goal states: 'Given a Premier case created at 17:00 London time on a Friday (Q39), when the first-response clock is read, then it is running on the EMEA calendar, shows 4 business hours remaining, does not tick over the weekend.' As built, First_Response_Premier carries <businessHours>US Support</businessHours> on the process AND on its <milestones> block, and a milestone's own businessHours is the most specific of the three sources the engine consults - so the EMEA calendar M4-S03's flow stamps onto Case.BusinessHoursId is overridden for milestone timing and reaches only the escalation clock, whose businessHoursSource is Case. Worked against the goal's own scenario: 17:00 Friday London is 12:00 New York; US Support is 08:00-20:00 New York, so 240 business minutes expire at 16:00 New York = 21:00 the same Friday London - after EMEA close, on the day of arrival, weekend untouched. All three of the goal's clauses fail. business-hours-and-holidays/references/gotchas.md #5 names this exact failure as the one it exists to prevent. O-M4S02-02 records the divergence precisely and names three remedies; what no step could do is compare it to the milestone's own acceptance goal, because no step reads milestones[].goal and no checker asserts against it.

evidence.grounded_in: plan.json milestones[M4].goal; decisions.md O-M4S02-02; artefacts/M4-S02/deploy-order.md section 4.4; skills/admin/business-hours-and-holidays/references/gotchas.md #5; artefacts/M4-S01/settings/BusinessHours.settings-meta.xml (US Support 08:00-20:00 America/New_York, EMEA Support 08:00-18:00 Europe/London)

findings.recommendation: Accept the divergence for this phase (O-M4S02-02 option a) AND amend plan.json's M4 goal to state what the build actually promises. Option (b) - a US and an EMEA process per tier - is a re-plan contradicting assumption A27 and quadruples the process count for a two-tier promise; option (c) - businessHoursSource Static on US Support - contradicts Q43's answered value and makes every EMEA case escalate on New York hours, worse than the divergence it fixes. A goal that promises an EMEA clock nobody built will mis-set M5's UAT script, the release note, and the first support manager who reads it. If the Process Owner says EMEA Premier must genuinely count on London hours, this is a re-plan - better discovered at this gate than in UAT.

findings.title: Nothing in the build selects First_Response_Premier over First_Response_Standard
findings.detail: The two processes differ only in minutesToComplete (240 vs 720). Which one a case enters is decided by the SlaProcessId on the Entitlement record its Account holds, and no step in this build creates an Entitlement, an EntitlementTemplate, or anything binding Account.Support_Tier__c to one process rather than the other. The flow's Get_Active_Entitlement filters on AccountId and Status = 'Active' with getFirstRecordOnly true and NO tier filter; an Account with two active entitlements gets whichever the query returns first. workbook/01-objects-and-fields.md CWB-OBJ-009 asserts the binding ('Support_Tier__c is what selects which of these two processes an account's entitlement points at') and M4-S02's deploy-order.md section 5 records that EntitlementTemplate is 'not in this phase' - so both halves are written down, in two different files, and neither says the binding is unimplemented. REQ-040 is therefore delivered as metadata that can express the promise, not as a mechanism that applies it.

evidence.grounded_in: the Get_Active_Entitlement recordLookups filters (AccountId, Status Active, getFirstRecordOnly true, no Support_Tier__c filter); artefacts/M4-S02/deploy-order.md section 5; workbook/01-objects-and-fields.md CWB-OBJ-009; traceability.md REQ-040

findings.recommendation: Record entitlement creation and its per-tier SlaProcessId as a data/Setup prerequisite with a named owner - cheapest and honest - or scope an EntitlementTemplate plus a tier-aware assignment in a later phase.

findings.title: The flow's Priority values resolve against nothing in this build
findings.detail: Assignment_Priority_High writes <stringValue>High</stringValue> and Assignment_Priority_Medium writes Medium. No standardValueSets/CasePriority exists anywhere under artefacts/ - verified by exhaustive grep and independently recorded by D-M4S03-03 and M3-S03's web-to-case-form-contract.md section 7. The contrast with CaseOrigin is the point: M1-S01 DID ship standardValueSets/CaseOrigin.standardValueSet-meta.xml because the build changes it; it did not ship CasePriority because the build does not, which is legitimate and is why this is classed unassertable rather than unresolved. But four separate places now depend on the target org's untouched CasePriority values with nothing able to assert them: this flow's two writes, M3-S03's two <casePriority>Medium</casePriority> intake defaults, M3-S01's Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save, and CaseMilestoneServiceTest.caseOverrides' 'Priority' => 'Medium'. If a target org has restricted or renamed CasePriority - a common hardening step - the flow writes an invalid value and the insert fails.

evidence.grounded_in: decisions.md D-M4S03-03 ('no CasePriority value set exists anywhere under artefacts/'); artefacts/M3-S03/settings/Case.settings-meta.xml lines 25, 35; artefacts/M3-S01/objects/Case/validationRules/Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save.validationRule-meta.xml

findings.recommendation: Either declare standardValueSets/CasePriority as an M5 output so the build asserts the three values it relies on, or record 'the target org's CasePriority still carries High and Medium' as a one-line pre-deploy check. Decide it together with gate decision item 6, which is the separate question of WHICH value each case should get.

findings.title: Between now and M5-S05, no manifest in this build carries M4-S05's Apex
findings.detail: The Apex exception is correctly applied: M4-S05 declares no package.xml because apex-builder's Output Contract names none, section 4 borrowed-agent condition 2 forbids declaring an output the owning agent does not produce, and the step's always-on manifest check correctly recorded skipped-not-applicable naming M5-S05. The gap is one of timing. M5-S05 is pending, so a manifest-mode validation of MILESTONE-M4-package.xml today deploys the entitlement processes, the milestone type and the before-save flow WITHOUT the trigger that completes their milestones - precisely the half-build the milestone goal's second sentence warns against. Mock deploy runs 1 to 4 used source mode, which copies the tree whole and therefore did include the Apex, which is why run 4 reached 55 components; a manifest-mode run of this file would deploy 8 members and no Apex. Same shape as F-18 (M2's stale merged manifest before any manifest-mode deploy): this build has now twice produced a merged manifest whose coverage differs from what the operator actually validated.

evidence.grounded_in: standards/build-orchestration.md section 5 'The Apex exception'; plan.json steps[M4-S05].acceptance_tests[2]; plan.json steps[M5-S05].status = pending; reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M4.md run 4 (source mode, 55 components)

findings.recommendation: Nothing required for the gate. State on the merged manifest and in M5's plan that MILESTONE-M4-package.xml is deliberately Apex-free and that M5-S05 closes it. Anyone wanting a manifest-mode dry run of M4 before M5-S05 must hand-add the four ApexClass and one ApexTrigger members; this agent did not, because inventing members the contract assigns to another step is what section 4 condition 2 forbids.

findings.title: The escalation's assignedToTemplate notification may reach nobody - the Tier 2 queue has no mailbox
findings.detail: Both escalation actions set assignedTo Tier_2_Engineering with assignedToTemplate case_intake/Case_Escalated_To_Tier2, a template that mails the NEW owner - the Tier 2 queue. But artefacts/M2-S04/queues/Tier_2_Engineering.queue-meta.xml has doesSendEmailToMembers false and NO <email> element at all. M4-S04's deploy-order.md U3 records this as UNVERIFIED at M4-S04's scope ('where an assignedToTemplate email goes when the target queue has no <email> and doesSendEmailToMembers is false'); the queue is M2-S04's artefact, so only a milestone-or-wider read can close it, and the answer is that the queue has no mailbox. The M2 gate already noted it from the other side ('checklist line 4 (Tier 2 mailbox) NOT ticked - artefact has no <email>') and D-M2S04-02 deliberately refused to invent an address. Nobody has composed the two. As built, REQ-023's 'Tier 2 receive Support cases that go untouched for 8 business hours' is delivered as an ownership change Tier 2 must discover from a list view - consistent with REQ-023's own 'pick work from a list' but not with REQ-033's 'Tier 2 receives a named handover notice'.

evidence.grounded_in: artefacts/M4-S04/escalationRules/Case.escalationRules-meta.xml (assignedToTemplate x2); artefacts/M4-S04/deploy-order.md U3; decisions.md D-M2S04-02; plan.json human_gates milestone:M2 notes ('checklist line 4 (Tier 2 mailbox) NOT ticked'); traceability.md REQ-023, REQ-033

findings.recommendation: Name a Tier 2 mailbox and add <email> to the queue - a one-line M2 amendment, which re-opens an accepted milestone, so weigh that - or accept that the handover notice reaches only the outgoing owner and record REQ-033 as half-delivered. Decide it in one pass with gate decision item 1, which is the same question for the Billing queue.

findings.title: A split deploy that ships position 8 before position 10 will fail its own Apex tests
findings.detail: Settings:Flow sets enableFlowDeployAsActiveEnabled true and the flow is <status>Active</status>, so a production deploy of an active flow runs the org's Apex tests (O-M4S03-02, quoting api_meta.txt L116877). The build's only test, CaseMilestoneServiceTest, is @IsTest(SeeAllData=true); requireActiveProcess() asserts an active SlaProcess exists and the first test method asserts an open First Response CaseMilestone was generated for a Case it inserts. Both depend on the position-10 entitlement process being in the org and active. O-M4S03-02 records the active-flow/Apex-test coupling; D-M4S05-04 records the test's org prerequisites; neither composes them with the deploy-order buckets, and the composition is where the risk lives. Inside one Metadata API request everything lands before tests run and the path is sound; across two requests ordered by the ten-slot sequence, position 8 runs tests position 10 has not yet satisfied and the deploy rolls back naming the Apex rather than the ordering. Smaller observation in the same class, not raised to its own finding: requireActiveProcess()'s SOQL is SELECT Id, Name FROM SlaProcess WHERE IsActive = true LIMIT 1 and does not filter on the process carrying a First Response milestone, though its assertion message says it must - the over-claim is caught one assertion later by the before.isEmpty() check, so the test still fails loudly rather than silently; the message is imprecise, not the logic.

evidence.grounded_in: decisions.md O-M4S03-02, D-M4S05-04; artefacts/M4-S03/settings/Flow.settings-meta.xml; workbook/06-automation.md CWB-AUT-022, CWB-AUT-028 (position 8) and CWB-AUT-015 to 017 (position 10); skills/devops/flow-deployment-activation-ordering

findings.recommendation: Deploy M4 as one Metadata API request, or state in the deploy-order note that positions 8 and 10 of this milestone must travel together to production. Shares one remedy with F-46 - decide both once.

findings.title: The position-8 flow reads by name the BusinessHours records position 10 creates
findings.detail: No metadata reference crosses backwards - CWB-AUT-026 records the direction explicitly and correctly ('the flow's conditions name fields from M1-S01 (deploy-time dependency) and read M4-S01/M4-S02 calendars and entitlement processes at run time only') - so nothing fails at deploy. But Get_EMEA_Support_Calendar and Get_US_Support_Calendar filter on Name at run time. In a split deploy, any Case created between request 8 and request 10 gets NO BusinessHoursId stamped, and the escalation rule's entry 2 (businessHoursSource Case) then falls back to the org default for those cases, silently. M4-S04's deploy-order.md U2 asks exactly this question - what entry 2 does when Case.BusinessHoursId is null - and leaves it UNVERIFIED.

evidence.grounded_in: the two BusinessHours recordLookups (filters on Name); workbook/06-automation.md CWB-AUT-026; artefacts/M4-S04/deploy-order.md U2

findings.recommendation: Same as F-45: one request, or an explicit statement that positions 8 and 10 travel together. The two findings share one remedy.

findings.title: The Billing-queue mail loop: notifyCaseOwner on a Billing-owned case posts into a live Email-to-Case intake address
findings.detail: Listed for register completeness; documented in full at O-M4S04-01 and presented as gate decision item 1. notifyCaseOwner is true on both escalation actions; the case owner at escalation time is whichever queue M3-S04's assignment rule chose; the Billing queue's <email> is billing@acme.example; and M3-S03 configures that same address as a live Email-to-Case routing address. An escalation notification to a Billing-owned case therefore posts into an intake address, creating a new case that escalates 480 minutes later and posts again. Severity is split deliberately: the rule ships <active>false</active> so nothing loops on deploy, making this LOW as deployed and HIGH the moment checklist line 4 is signed. F-36's fix is what made it real - before notifyToTemplate was added, notifyCaseOwner could not send mail at all. Recorded here at P2 as the as-deployed severity; the activation severity is stated in the report.

evidence.grounded_in: decisions.md O-M4S04-01 (closing O-M3S04-02), D-M2S04-04, D-M4S04-01; artefacts/M3-S03/settings/Case.settings-meta.xml line 32; artefacts/M4-S04/escalation-activation-runbook.md section 4 R2

findings.recommendation: O-M4S04-01 option (c) - give the Billing queue a notification address that is not an intake address - paired with F-44's Tier 2 mailbox as ONE decision, because both are the same question (which mailboxes do these queues notify) deferred for the same reason. If no address is forthcoming, choose option (b) and record explicitly that escalation is a silent ownership change this phase, so M5's UAT script tests for a list-view handover rather than an email.

order_of_execution.why_they_never_contend: The flow is <triggerType>RecordBeforeSave</triggerType> with <recordTriggerType>Create</recordTriggerType> - insert only. The trigger is 'on Case (after update)' - update only. No contention, no double-write, and triggerOrder 10 has nothing to order against (this is the build's only record-triggered flow on Case, so checker rule 8 is satisfied by its presence rather than by a conflict).
order_of_execution.insert: The before-save flow runs ahead of Apex before-triggers and ahead of custom validation rules, stamping EntitlementId, BusinessHoursId and Priority. Two consequences the build depends on: (1) Priority_Required_On_Agent_Save (M3-S01) evaluates AFTER the stamp, so a web case with no Priority is rescued rather than rejected - this is the closure of F-32 that the M3 gate's decision (2) anticipated and could not prove because M4-S03 did not exist, and it is now proven at the artefact level; (2) entitlement rules run near the END of the insert's order of execution, after all before AND after triggers, so CaseMilestone rows created by this save are invisible to any trigger inside it. The trigger's own header comment records this, and it is why 'after update' is a correctness requirement rather than a style choice.
order_of_execution.first_update_out_of_new: The after-update trigger fires, the CaseMilestone rows created by the insert already exist, the three-clause WHERE (case Ids AND milestone type AND CompletionDate = NULL) finds the open one, and one DML writes CompletionDate.
order_of_execution.idempotency: CompletionDate = NULL in the same WHERE makes a second pass a no-op, which is the guard that substitutes for the recursion control the two-file shape does not have (D-M4S05-03).
order_of_execution.the_one_real_interaction_runs_forwards: The escalation rule's entry 2 uses businessHoursSource Case, reading Case.BusinessHoursId - the field the flow stamped during the SAME insert, before the escalation engine sees the record. Forwards, not backwards.

g4_decision_items.title: The R2 Billing-queue mail loop, with its three remedies
g4_decision_items.recommendation: Option (c) - give the Billing queue a notification address that is not an intake address - PAIRED WITH F-44's Tier 2 mailbox as one decision, because both are the same question (which mailboxes do these queues notify) deferred for the same reason (D-M2S04-02 refused to invent an address, correctly). Option (a) is cleanest technically and most likely wrong - it silently drops a whole queue out of an SLA requirement.md states unqualified. Option (b) is WEAKENED BY F-44: the assignedToTemplate recipient is the Tier 2 queue, which has no mailbox, so choosing (b) today means NEITHER notification reaches anyone. If no address is forthcoming, choose (b) and record explicitly that escalation is a silent ownership change this phase, so M5's UAT script tests for a list-view handover rather than an email.

g4_decision_items.title: Entitlement settings owned by no step
g4_decision_items.recommendation: Option (b) - record it as a named deploy prerequisite, not a plan amendment. Three reasons: it is the same shape the M3 gate already accepted for F-28, so the build has a precedent and a place to keep it; enabling Entitlement Management is a one-time org-lifetime action that does not belong in a per-release manifest; and amending an M4 step's outputs[] now would force a rebuild of a documented step for a file that changes nothing about the artefacts already proven. The gate must record a named owner, a date, and BOTH switches - enableEntitlements before anything in M4 deploys, enableMilestoneStoppedTime before go-live rather than after the first SLA dispute (gotchas.md #10). F-39 widens the blast radius from M4-S02's two files to three of M4's five steps.

g4_decision_items.title: The Q51 calendar divergence
g4_decision_items.recommendation: Option (a) accept the divergence for this phase, AND amend plan.json's M4 goal to match. This is the item that matters most, because it is the one the milestone's own goal contradicts (F-40). Option (b) is a re-plan contradicting A27 and quadruples the process count for a two-tier promise; option (c) contradicts Q43's answered value and makes every EMEA case escalate on New York hours, worse than the divergence it fixes. Option (a) costs nothing to build and everything to FORGET, which is exactly why the goal text must change with it - a goal promising an EMEA clock nobody built will mis-set M5's UAT script, the release note, and the first support manager who reads it. If the Process Owner says EMEA Premier must genuinely count on London hours, this is a re-plan, better discovered at this gate than in UAT.

g4_decision_items.title: The 720 and 480 placeholder numbers
g4_decision_items.recommendation: Confirm both at the gate; neither is a blocker. The builder was right to refuse to invent either - a builder-composed number reads as a customer commitment nobody made. Two things to put to the Process Owner in the same breath: (1) the 720 derivation is COUPLED to the US Support calendar's 12-hour day, so if decision item 3 ever moves Standard onto EMEA hours (10 open hours) the '1 business day' figure becomes 600, not 720 - one decision silently changes the other; (2) a Severity 1 outage escalating on the SAME 480 as a routine case is the reading most likely to surprise a support manager reading the rule for the first time. Each fix is one integer in one file.

g4_decision_items.title: The seeded holidays and the Q90 owner
g4_decision_items.recommendation: The OWNER half is the one to close at this gate; the holiday list can follow. An unnamed owner is the more corrosive of the two - a calendar with wrong holidays fails visibly on a known date, while a calendar with no owner silently stops pausing in a year and nobody is accountable for noticing. Name the individual at this gate and give them the runbook's section 4 yearly procedure plus a date to replace the seed with Acme's real list before production. Do NOT let the 14-entry seed deploy to production as-is: it is the right shape and the wrong data, and it is convincing enough to be mistaken for confirmed by anyone who reads the calendar rather than the runbook. Same restraint D-M4S01-02 exercised in refusing to invent a name, carried one step further.

g4_decision_items.title: The Priority value mapping
g4_decision_items.recommendation: Confirm the first two rows (Severity 1 -> High, grounded in requirement.md L18 the only unconditional urgency statement; everything else -> Medium, consistent with M3-S03's intake default) and put the PREMIER row specifically to the Process Owner. Conflating 'contractually faster' with 'more urgent' is a real design claim: it means a routine Premier question outranks a Standard customer's production problem in every priority-sorted list view and report M5 builds. The builder says so itself - this is the weakest of the three rows. If the answer is that tier should not drive Priority, the fix is to delete one <rules> condition, and the SLA difference still lands because it comes from the entitlement process not from Priority. Decide it TOGETHER WITH F-42: item 6 is which value, F-42 is whether the target org still carries that value at all.

g4_decision_items.title: The completion-signal proxy
g4_decision_items.recommendation: RAISE THIS ABOVE THE OTHER EIGHT. It is the only item where the built behaviour can make a FALSE SLA CLAIM - a milestone reported met on a case no customer heard from. Both error directions are live and the first will happen constantly: M4-S04's escalation changes ownership, and an agent handling that case will move it off New, completing the first-response milestone with no reply sent. Two things make it cheap to fix if the Process Owner wants Q50's literal signal: the rule lives in one @TestVisible constant (OPENING_STATUS) so changing WHICH status is a one-line edit, but moving to the first outbound EmailMessage is a DIFFERENT artefact (an after-insert trigger on EmailMessage filtered to Incoming = false) which this step's outputs[] does not declare and which is therefore a plan amendment plus a rebuild, not an edit. If the answer is 'accept the proxy this phase', record it as an explicit dated acceptance with the false-positive direction named, and put a line in M5's UAT script that watches for milestones completed on cases with no outbound email.

g4_decision_items.title: The two-file trigger shape
g4_decision_items.recommendation: Accept for this phase. This is the WEAKEST of the nine items and should take the least gate time. The idempotency guard (CompletionDate = NULL in the query, asserted by skipsAMilestoneThatIsAlreadyCompleted) is domain-correct and arguably stronger than a recursion counter for a trigger that fires once in a Case's life; the trigger does no DML on Case so it cannot re-enter itself; and the alternative - shipping four framework classes nobody asked for - enlarges the deploy for a benefit the build cannot use. The builder's reasoning was mechanically verified: a plan-wide search found TriggerControl=0, ApplicationLogger=0, Trigger_Setting__mdt=0, TriggerHandler=1, the one occurrence being this step's own templates[] citation. Record it as a planner v6 backlog item (a shared 'Apex foundations' step owning TestDataFactory, TriggerHandler, TriggerControl and ApplicationLogger, with every Apex step depending on it) rather than as an M4 remedy - D-M4S05-05 already names that step for a different reason, so ONE backlog item closes both.

g4_decision_items.title: The RTM's three residual orphans - CLOSED, nothing to decide
g4_decision_items.recommendation: Record the closure and move on. check_rtm.py v1.1.5 landed today (0c585e185) and the build-scope re-run reports 47 rows, 0 coverage gaps, 0 orphans, 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0. The three ApexClass orphans were a checker limitation, they were correctly dispositioned REVIEW rather than papered over, and the fix went into the skill rather than into the matrix. The only residue is stale prose in traceability.md (F-48), which the doc keeper rewrites at its next touch. Worth one sentence at the gate because it is the fourth instalment of one skill-depth fix (v1.1.2 -> v1.1.5) driven entirely by this build's doc-keeper runs - the flywheel producing exactly what it is for.

extensions.optional_command_note: OPTIONAL and HUMAN-RUN. This agent ran neither, ran no sf command at all, ran no mock_deploy.py, and made no org contact. The sandbox form is a dry run; the production form is documented production-only, requires Apex tests and returns a job id for a later quick deploy - naming the right one matters, because offering the production form for a sandbox sends the human into an error that has nothing to do with their build. Three things to know before running either, none of which the command will tell you: this manifest carries NO Apex (F-43); the target org must already have Entitlement Management enabled (F-39); and the production form runs Apex tests, and this build's only test needs an active SlaProcess the same deploy is creating (F-45).
extensions.set_milestone_command: python3 scripts/build_plan.py set-milestone .sfskills/builds/case-onboarding/plan.json M4 --status verified --report-path reports/MILESTONE-M4-REPORT.md
extensions.set_milestone_result: milestone M4: status -> verified, report -> reports/MILESTONE-M4-REPORT.md. The only write this agent made to plan.json, made through the subcommand, no JSON hand-edited. 'verified' is a statement about what the checks found, not an approval - the gate record stays empty until a human writes it.
extensions.gate_command_note: Printed, never run. gate is the only writer of a gate decision and a human is the only decider. Returning the line is not approving it.

gate_conditions.every_step_documented_or_blocked_with_a_: yes - all five documented, NO blocked step, so approving this gate accepts no step-level gap. Unlike M3's gate, which was signed over the blocked M3-S05.

extensions.nothing_else_touched: No artefact, no tests/<step>/results.json, no step status, no gate record, no decisions.md, no traceability.md, no workbook file, no PLAN.md, no CLARIFICATIONS.md, and nothing outside this build directory.
extensions.persistence_deviation: agents/_shared/DELIVERABLE_CONTRACT.md also calls for a markdown/JSON pair at docs/reports/milestone-verifier/<run_id>.{md,json}. This invocation scoped writes to the build directory, which is the --no-persist case: the build-scoped envelope under envelopes/M4/ and its markdown twin carry the same content, and the structured envelope is returned in the run output. Recorded rather than left as a silent omission.
extensions.severity_mapping_note: The report uses the build's HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW convention; the envelope schema's findings[].severity enum is P0/P1/P2/INFO. Mapping used: HIGH -> P1, MEDIUM -> P2, LOW -> INFO. No P0 is used, because a P0 would contradict a ready-with-findings verdict. F-47 carries its as-deployed severity (P2, the rule ships inactive) and its on-activation severity is stated in the finding detail rather than by inflating the enum value.
